page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard3.Flex.56-224 is a compute-oriented virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It is driven by an Intel Xeon 8358 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The configuration allocates 56 dedicated physical processor cores and 112 vCPUs via two threads per core, paired with 224.0 GB of system memory. This yields a ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, aligning the instance with compute-intensive workloads that require substantial parallel thread execution rather than excessive memory footprints.

Hardware resource distribution on the VM.Standard3.Flex.56-224 includes no integrated local storage and zero GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage volumes for persistent data needs. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Because dedicated vCPU allocations avoid noisy neighbor interference, CPU resource consistency remains stable during prolonged processing cycles across all 112 threads.

From an architectural standpoint, the instance balances massive compute capacity against a moderate memory pool, making it cost-efficient for parallel execution jobs where memory density does not need to scale to traditional enterprise 1:4 or 1:8 allocations. Primary workloads suitable for this instance encompass multi-threaded compilation, batch data processing, distributed compute clustering, scientific modeling, and high-concurrency microservices architectures.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard3.Flex.56-224 is an x86_64 virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8358 processor clocked at 2.6 GHz. Configured with 56 dedicated physical cores and 112 vCPUs via two threads per core, it offers 224.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio tailored for compute-heavy applications. The server features no local storage and no dedicated hardware GPUs, relying on remote block storage solutions for disk operations. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is included. Due to its dedicated processor allocation, the instance delivers sustained compute performance without CPU oversubscription contention. The VM.Standard3.Flex.56-224 is structured for high-throughput batch compute, parallel code building, continuous integration pipelines, video transcoding, and compute-bound container clusters requiring high core density without excessive per-core memory overhead.
